Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February,

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:17629
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 2568 of 2023

Appellant :- Rahul And 3 Others
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Appellant :- Anil Kumar Tiwari,Jitendra Singh,Radhey Shyam Shukla,Vipul Shuk
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Sunil Kumar Srivastava
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (1) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention
of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellants - Rahul, Hukum Singh, Neeraj and Beenu
against the summoning order dated 22.4.2022 passed by the Special Judge (Sc/St Act),
Shahjahanpur in Complaint Case No. 138 of 2019, arising out of case crime no. 5 of 2019, under
Sections 376-D, 323, 504 Ipc and 3(2)(5) Sc/St Act, P.S. Katra, District Shahjahanpur.
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 as well as the learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that the impugned order is not sustainable under law and the same has been passed in an arbitrary manner avoiding absolutely the mandatory provisions of law.
It is further submitted that the learned trial court did not consider the aspect of submission of final report in this matter.

As a matter of fact, the Investigating Officer of Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36221591/
1

entities.text: Investigating Officer of Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: this case found absolutely no evidence against the present appellants and all the allegations levelled against them were found false during investigation and that is why the investigation culminated into closure report.

It is also submitted that although the summoning order was passed in a complaint case but the evidence on record, which was already collected by the I.O. of this case, was not liable to be ignored completely.
The medical evidence does not corroborate the prosecution version.
It is also submitted that on the basis of insufficient and unreliable evidence, the impugned summoning order was passed by the trial court.

It is further submitted that withuot there being any specific allegation the case in hand was made a matter of gang rape and the elder persons of the family have also been implicated in an offence like gang rape.
It is also submitted that the appellant nos. 2,3 and 4 were not present on the spot at the time of the alleged incident but the trial court ignored this material fact as well.

It is also submitted that the victim of this case in her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC does not utter anything contrary to the defence but when after rejecting the final report the protest petition was treated as complaint case and evidence of the victim was recorded, she took a total u-turn and made some inconsistent statements than that of her earlier statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC.
It it lastly submitted that the impugned summoning order is not sustainable under law and is liable to be quashed.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 and the learned AGA vehemently opposed the prayer and submitted that it is a case of gang rape which has been committed with the answering respondent no.2 by the present appellants.
It is also submitted that the appellants were quite aware of the fact that the victim belonged to the SC/ST community.

It is further submitted that the I.O. of this case conducted the investigation in an arbitrary and illegal manner and closure report was submitted in the matter deliberately by suppressing the real facts and evidence relating to this case and that is why the closure report was questioned by the complainant by way of filing the protest petition and negotiating the same the learned trial court rejected the final report submitted by the police and the protest petition was treated as a criminal complaint.

It is further submitted that in a criminal complaint the trial court has to peruse the evidence rendered by the complainant under Sections 200 and 202 CrPC and other materials on record made available by the complainant and the trial court proceeded in the right direction by following the legal norms set to be adhered to at the time of passing the summoning order.
There is no infirmity, illegality or perversity in the impugned order warranting interference by this Court.
5. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned summoning order carefully.

6. It is trite law that while passing an order on the point of summoning the accused in a private criminal complaint case the Magistrate is under legal obligation to act on the basis of evidence under Section 200 and 202 CrPC and other materials on record put forth by the complainant and inquiry,
if any, conducted by the Court itself as to whether there exists sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused or not.

7. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Kewal Krishan s/o Lachman Das vs. Suraj Bhan and another, AIR 1980 SC 1780 on the subject held like this :
Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36221591/

entities.text: Kewal Krishan s/o Lachman Das vs. Suraj Bhan and another, AIR 1980 SC 1780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 "At the stage of Section 203 and 204, Criminal Procedure Code in a case exclusively triable by the Court of Session, all that the Magistrate has to do is to see whether on a cursory perusal of the complaint and the evidence recorded during the preliminary inquiry under Sections 200 and 202, Criminal Procedure Code, there is prima facie evidence in support of the charge leveled against the accused.
All that he has to see is whether or not there is "sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
At this stage, the Magistrate is not to weigh the evidence meticulously as if he were the trial court.
The standard to be adopted by the Magis trate in scrutinising the evidence is not the same as the one which is to be kept in view at the stage of framing charges.

This Court has held in Ramesh Singh's case (ibid), that even at the stage of framing;
charges the truth, veracity and effect of the evidence which the complainant produces or proposes to adduce at the trial, is not to be meticulously judged.
The standard of proof and judgment, which is to be applied finally before finding the accused guilty or otherwise, is not exactly to be applied at the stage of framing charges.

A fortiori, at the stage of Sections 202/204, if there is prima facie evidence in support of the allegations in the complaint relating to a case exclusively triable by the Court of Session, that will be a sufficient ground for issuing process to the accused and committing them for trial to the Court of Session."

8. Hence, the satisfaction of the Magistrate for issuing process under Section 204 CrPC is a condition precedent based upon the examination of the complainant and his witnesses or by some inquiry contemplated under Section 202 CrPC.

It is to be remembered that the Magistrate is never under legal obligation to pass a detailed order at the juncture of issuing summons to the accused and this legal dictum has been recognized by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in U.P. Pollution Control Board vs. M/s Mohan Meakins Ltd. and others, AIR 2000 SC 1456.

entities.text: U.P. Pollution Control Board vs. M/s Mohan Meakins Ltd. and others, AIR 2000 SC 1456
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, if the Magistrate proceeds to dismiss the complaint, he has to record the reasons in such situation.

9. So far as the case in hand is concerned, the complainant in her statement under Section 200 CrPC has made a categorical statement that at the time of the incident, her daughter, the victim, was dragged into the field by accused Rahul with the help of other co-accused persons Neeraj, Hukum Singh and Beenu and gang rape was committed with her by accused persons Rahul and Neeraj and she was caught hold by other co-accused persons Hukum Singh and Beenu.
On the noise made by her daughter, her sons Avon and Ramsagar came over there and accused Rahul was caught on the spot and the rest accused persons fled away.
The said accused Rahul was handed over to the police.
The prosecutrix was also beaten by all the accused persons.

The victim was medically examined and F.I.R. was lodged at the police station and prior to that the accused persons Naresh, Pappu, Mahesh and Deepak Rai came to the house of the complainant and hurled abuses by caste related remarks.
She has also clarified that she belongs to SC/ST community.

10. Further, the statement of the victim herself was recorded under Section 202 CrPC wherein she narrated the same story, as PW-1 states and specific allegation for committing rape with her by accused Rahul and Neeraj with the help of other co-accused persons Hukum Singh and Beenu has been levelled by her.
She also states that accused persons belonged to backward class.

Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36221591/
3 11.

entities.text: Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Statements of Avon and Ramsagar, brothers of the victim, were also recorded under Section 202 CrPC wherein they corroborated the version made by the complainant under Section 200 CrPC and the victim herself in her statement under Section 202 CrPC.

Both the witnesses explicitly state that they had reached the place of occurrence and accused Rahul was held on the spot and subsequently the other accused persons came to their house and threatened them by caste related remarks.

12. In the course of enquiry, the concerned Magistrate recorded statement of Dr. Tanvi Agrawal under Section 202 CrPC who states in her statement that on 9.1.2019 at 4.10 a.m. while she was working as Medical Officer in District Hospital, Shahjahanpur, she medically examined the victim of this case and got that hymen was old torn and no sign for use of force was found on her private part but however sign of force was found on the face of the victim.

She further states that as per the pathology report, no spermatozoa dead or alive in the vaginal smear was found and five contusions were found over the face of the victim which denote the fight and protest made by her.

13. The learned Magistrate analysed the aforesaid statements under Section 200 and 202 CrPC and found that Naresh, Pappu, Mahesh, Deepak and Raju appeared to be falsely implicated in this matter because in the written report given at the police station the name of any of them had not been mentioned whereas the written report was given at the police station by the mother of the victim herself.

On that basis the Magistrate concerned did not find any ground to summon Naresh,
Pappu, Mahesh, Deepak and Raju in this case but relying upon the statements made by the complainant under Section 200 CrPC and that of the victim, her two brothers and the doctor under Section 202 CrPC

, the Magistrate recorded his prima facie satisfaction to pass the summoning order in respect of the accused persons Rahul, Hukum Singh, Neeraj and Beenu to face trial under Sections 376D, 323, 504 IPC and 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act.

14. The learned counsel for the appellants has vehemently argued that during course of entire investigation the I.O. of the case found no evidence at all against the present appellants and the whole prosecution story made by the complainant was found to be false and fabricated.
It has been emphasized upon that in her statement under Section 164 CrPC the victim herself does not support the prosecution version and the medical evidence falsifies the prosecution story.

15. However, it is to be kept in mind that the stand of the complainant has been specific by way of filing the protest petition wherein it was alleged that the investigation in this case was not conducted properly, fairly and in legal manner.

It has been alleged in the protest petition that the final report in this case has been filed by ignoring the established legal norms and the victim was threatened as well by the lady police and compelled to give statement in favour of the accused persons and in this respect she has already given an affidavit to the I.O. which was never made part of the case diary.
Since the complainant already questioned the proceeding of investigation, there is no justification to rely upon the evidence and material collected by the I.O. during investigation.

The fact, which is not to be forgotten, is that the order of the Magistrate whereby the final report submitted by the police was rejected and the protest petition submitted by the complainant was treated as complaint has not been challenged by the accused appellants.
The order under challenge is only the summoning order which was passed by the Magistrate concerned.

Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36221591/
4 16.

entities.text: Rahul And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as the plea taken by the learned counsel for the appellants that all the four accused persons belong to the same family and out of them, three accused persons are real brothers and it is not plausible and natural that three real brothers committed rape with a lady at the same time in front of each other is concerned
, I do not find any force in the said contention.

17. Learned AGA in this context has vehemently submitted that there is no allegation of actual rape against the accused appellant Hukum Singh and Beenu, who are real brothers but actual participation in the crime has been alleged against accused appellants Rahul and Neeraj.
Since Hukum Singh and Beenu were aiding in the commission of the crime they were also acting in furtherance of common intention of all.

18. Another specific plea has been taken by the learned counsel for the appellants that accused appellants 2,3 and 4, namely, Hukum Singh, Neeraj and Beenu were not present on the spot at the time of commission of the crime.

19. Advancing a plea of alibi in their respect, statement of independent witness Ved Ram Pal has been emphasized upon who states that on the date of the occurrence the appellant Hukum Singh was in the market, appellant Neeraj was on his duty at Billpur Railway Station from 8.00 a.m. to 8.00 p.m. and appellant Beenu was present in Swami Nand Kishore Acharya Bal Vidhyalay,
Miranpur, Katra till 4.00 p.m. and all the three accused were not present in the village.

entities.text: Swami Nand Kishore Acharya Bal Vidhyalay
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text:
However,
the said statement was recorded by the Investigating Officer during investigation of this case whereas it has been impressed upon earlier that the complainant filed a protest petition against all the evidence collected by the I.O. during investigation which she claims to be false and fabricated.

20. The Magistrate concerned in this matter has utilized its power to take cognizance of the offence on the basis of complaint alleged to have been committed by the accused on the basis of relevant evidence under Sections 200 and 202 CrPC.

It is always to be kept in mind that at the time of summoning of the accused in a complaint case the Magistrate has to be satisfied whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding and not sufficient ground for conviction because the adequacy of evidence for supporting the conviction can be determined only at the stage of trial and not at the stage of inquiry and the Magistrate is not required even to record reasons at the stage of issuing process to the accused, as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in Jagdish Ram vs. State of Rajasthan and another, (2004) 4 SCC 432.
21.

entities.text: Jagdish Ram vs. State of Rajasthan and another, (2004) 4 SCC 432
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above discussion, I am of the opinion that there is no illegality, perversity or infirmity in the impugned summoning order passed by the Magistrate concerned.

Sufficient materials were available before the Magistrate concerned to summon the accused appellants to face trial under Sections 376D, 323, 504 IPC and 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act on the basis of evidence under Sections 200 and 202 CrPC and other materials placed on record by the complainant and no illegality has been committed by the Magistrate concerned in passing the same.
The appeal lacks merits and is liable to be dismissed and the same is accordingly dismissed.
